clue.text: Breezy crossword solutions which illuminate dark passages

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the things that light up gloomy hallways, so it works as a plural noun

parts.note: a fan is what makes a breeze, so breezy suggests the device
lights is the solver's term for the entries written into a grid

explanation.surface: Airy puzzle answers that shed light on obscure bits of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark passages' pretends to be baffling sentences; it means unlit corridors.
explanation.definitionFit: Semicircular windows set over doors let daylight into otherwise gloomy hallways.

clue.text: Decrees that this book follow the Gospel story

definitions.meaning: laws or enactments passed by a parliament

definitions.text: this book follow the Gospel story
definitions.meaning: the New Testament book coming straight after the four Gospels

explanation.surface: Rulings that place a particular book after the life of Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes passed by parliament are enactments; the Acts of the Apostles is the Bible book placed after John's Gospel.

clue.text: Prescribe what to do with immature wine

definitions.meaning: to stipulate or set out as a rule

definitions.text: what to do with immature wine
definitions.meaning: young wine is stored in a cellar to mature

explanation.surface: A doctor's orders about what to do with a young vintage.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out a rule is to stipulate it; young bottles are cellared on their sides to age.

clue.text: A flowery tribute for the star of "the Wizard of oz""

definitions.meaning: a wreath or ring of blossoms given in honour

definitions.text: the star of "the Wizard of oz"
definitions.meaning: Judy, who played Dorothy in the 1939 film

explanation.surface: Floral honours for the lead actress of a famous film.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of blooms is an honour; Judy of that surname starred as Dorothy in the 1939 musical film.

clue.text: Objection raised to a musical instrument

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is written upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: but is an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: Someone protests at an instrument being brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BUT into TUB, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The large low-pitched brass instrument of a band or orchestra.

clue.text: Deeming art and design to be very popular

indicators.note: to design is to plan and arrange, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone judges art and design to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' looks like part of the subject matter but tells you to rearrange DEEMING ART AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widely sought after by many people is popular.

clue.text: Turn up at work with a ous toms declaration

definitions.meaning: to present yourself for your job or shift
telling customs officers about goods on which tax is payable

explanation.surface: Arriving at the office having filled in a form at the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenting yourself for a shift is arriving at work; telling customs officers about taxable goods is declaring them.

clue.text: A vexed question for the escapologist

definitions.meaning: a difficult, tangled issue
an escape artist's literal difficulty is the tied rope

explanation.surface: A tricky issue for a performer who wriggles out of bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangled, intricate difficulty; for an escape artist the tied rope is literally the difficulty.

clue.text: South American doctor gets a first-class return in a Panamanian port

indicators.note: in means the doctor and the reversed letters go inside the port

parts.note: Colon is the port at the Caribbean end of the Panama Canal
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A doctor from South America gets a top-class return ticket to a port in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns AI (A1, first-class) into IA; MB and IA go 'in' COLON.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the country of Bogota, in South America.

clue.text: Frank got fed up with being a competitor

parts.note: frank and candid both mean open and honest
ate up means consumed, finished eating

explanation.surface: An honest person grew weary of being a contestant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like boredom; it is eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing for election or a job is a contender.

clue.text: Giant about to follow a gigantic king

indicators.note: to follow means this piece comes after the king

parts.note: Og, King of Bashan, is a giant in the Old Testament
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A huge figure is on the point of succeeding a towering monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to follow' reads as 'soon to follow'; it is RE placed after OG, the Biblical giant king.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating monster of folk tales is huge in size.

clue.text: Always make a charge

definitions.meaning: split as for aye, an old phrase meaning for ever
to rush out in a raid or attack

explanation.surface: Someone who constantly levies fees.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words the answer is 'for ay(e)', an old phrase meaning for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into two old words it means for ever; as one word it is a raid or attacking sally.

clue.text: Summary of notes produced by firm American lawyer

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A company and a US attorney draw up a summing-up of memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests memos; it means music, and the answer is the closing passage of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The concluding section of a musical piece rounds off the movement.

clue.text: High-flyer joins a sanctimonious sect

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
a lot is a group or set of people

explanation.surface: An ambitious achiever signs up with a self-righteous religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests a go-getter; it is literal, someone who flies aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman who flies the plane goes high in the sky.

clue.text: A birthday honour the Queen pinned on, by gum

indicators.note: pinned on means this letter is attached at the end

parts.note: MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is given in the Birthday Honours list
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The monarch pins a birthday award on someone, by golly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by gum' is an old exclamation like 'by golly'; here gum is the definition. The Birthday Honours are the awards Britain announces on the monarch's official birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: Fossilised tree resin, a hardened gum.

clue.text: Speech appealing for stringent measures

parts.note: O is the exclamation of an appeal, as in 'O Lord'
to ration is to impose strict limits on supplies

explanation.surface: A speaker pleading for austerity.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal address delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Thomas goes back into action, but with lower rank

indicators.note: into means the reversed name goes inside the action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: goes back means the name is read from right to left

parts.note: Tom is short for Thomas

explanation.surface: Thomas returns to the fighting, but now a lower rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' turns TOM into MOT, which goes 'into' DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reduced in status after a downgrade holds a lesser position.

clue.text: County town providing retirement facility for an old copper

parts.note: a bed is where you retire for the night
d was the old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A town offering a retirement home for an aged policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' is going to bed, not leaving work; 'old copper' is the pre-1971 penny, abbreviated d, not a policeman. Bedford is the county town of Bedfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The administrative centre of Bedfordshire, an English county.

clue.text: Notedly more eccentric member of the band

parts.note: D is one of the musical notes
rum means odd, so rummer is odder

explanation.surface: A stranger musician in the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist in a group keeps the beat on the kit.

clue.text: Body building drug editors crack up

indicators.note: to crack up is to break apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Journalists go mad over a performance-enhancing substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic compounds are used to build muscle mass.

clue.text: Discussion group in the airmen's mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: A talk held in the RAF dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the forces' dining room but signals a jumble of AIRMEN'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A class meeting for academic debate on a topic.

clue.text: They're handed to members of the forces

definitions.text: They're handed to members of the forces

parts.words: They're handed to members of the forces
parts.note: weapons issued to soldiers, and also the limbs that end in hands

explanation.surface: Kit given out to soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons are issued to soldiers; the limbs also have hands at their ends.

clue.text: As a card-player he's a sucker

definitions.meaning: the exposed partner hand in bridge
a baby's rubber teat, a pacifier

explanation.surface: A gambler who is easily fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the declarer's partner lays the hand face up. British English uses the word for a baby's pacifier.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge declarer's partner's hand laid face up; also a baby's rubber pacifier.

clue.text: Article the French said was a passage of mine

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
dit is French for said

explanation.surface: A French report described a tunnel in a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance tunnel driven into a mine.

clue.text: Where traders sell or give away

definitions.meaning: a retail premises
to inform on or betray someone

explanation.surface: Merchants either deal or hand things over free.
explanation.definitionFit: A retail outlet is where goods are sold; to inform on someone to the police is to betray them.

clue.text: Rummage for food

definitions.meaning: to dig or search about
slang for things to eat

explanation.surface: Scrabbling around for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig about searching; also slang for things to eat.

clue.text: Less than half are under age

definitions.meaning: forming the smaller group
legally a minor, not yet an adult

explanation.surface: Most of the group are adults.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the smaller share of a group; also, punningly, still a legal minor below adulthood.

clue.text: The type of meat served by frugal wives

parts.note: spare means meagre or frugal
ribs is joking slang for wives, from Eve being made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: Thrifty wives dish up cheap cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pork cuts from the lower part of the ribcage.
